Looking at my land and what I've always done, I need to think through the season carefully.

My 20 mu breaks down this way in my head: I have my wheat-maize rotation land — that's the backbone, probably 15 mu — and then I have my stevia plot, around 5 mu, which I grow under contract with the purchasing company out of the county town. The stevia contract gives me guaranteed income, so I keep that stable.

For the wheat, I'll plant in mid-October like always. I'll use Jimai 22 — it does well here in Quzhou and the seed station has it. I put down phosphorus and potash before planting, then split my nitrogen — some at planting, more at jointing. Water is my main cost since I pump from the well, but wheat needs it. I'll irrigate at jointing, heading, and grain filling. Three times is usually enough unless it's a dry spring.

For the summer maize after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed into the stubble — saves time, and some of my family is working in the city so I can't spend too long on land prep. I'll use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, same as my neighbors. Maize gets the summer rains mostly, so maybe one or two irrigations at most if July is dry. I apply urea in two splits.

For the stevia, the company tells me what variety to use. I'll till in spring, transplant the cuttings, and harvest the leaves twice before frost. Stevia needs more frequent watering because the roots are shallow, so I'll irrigate more often. Pesticide applications are important to protect leaf quality for the buyer.

My inputs are what they've always been — I'm not going to change much. I know my land.
